# SHARED LOWER-BOUND CORPUS (task 1.5-h).
#
# ITS OWN INVENTORY, NOT AN EXTENSION OF THE COUNT CORPUS. The upper table proves each site's
# ceiling with an N/N+1 pair. Extending it mechanically with one empty row per site would
# assert eight independent proofs where the implementations provide far fewer: several local
# emptiness predicates are SHADOWED by a later check that refuses the same input. This file
# therefore carries a different question -- what does the BOUNDARY do, and what would removing
# the local arm actually change -- and states the second answer per runtime.
#
# TWO CONTROLS PER RULE. `zero` refused alone does not pin a minimum of 1: an implementation
# tightened to demand two elements refuses zero exactly as before. `one` ACCEPTED is what makes
# the pair a bound rather than a prohibition.
#
# THE `*_removal` COLUMNS ARE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and they say what a row can and cannot
# prove in that runtime:
#
#   admits    removing the local arm ADMITS the empty input. The arm is load-bearing and the
#             row kills its removal outright.
#   crashes   removing it CRASHES the public validator on attacker-supplied input. Load-bearing;
#             the row kills its removal.
#   retags    the boundary still refuses, under a DIFFERENT reason. A row asserting the exact
#             refusal reason kills the removal; one asserting "refused" does not.
#   silent    the boundary still refuses under the SAME reason, because a later gate catches it.
#             NO verdict-based row can kill the removal. The row records boundary behaviour and
#             claims nothing about the local arm.
#   combined  the runtime has no separable zero arm to remove -- the emptiness case is one
#             conjunct of a single predicate that also enforces the ceiling and the declared
#             count. Nothing to mutate independently, so nothing is claimed.
#   n/a       no peer in that runtime; `owner` names who builds it.
#
# NORMATIVE SOURCES, one per rule, none re-authored here:
#   * plan page list and ranges-per-page  -- the residual-bounds table's minimum column.
#   * classification spans per page       -- "Every page SHALL carry AT LEAST ONE span".
#   * recovery manifest page list         -- authored by THIS task; it was the only gap. The
#                                            shared ceiling was stated for a recovery manifest
#                                            but its minimum spoke for the PLAN list alone.
#   * signed tombstone declared count     -- authored by THIS task, a DECLARED SCALAR rule.
#
# `MaxSweepHostsPerBatch` IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE. The bounds table gives it NO minimum, and both
# runtimes admit zero hosts. It is not a gap and SHALL NOT be added here.
#
# THE DECLARED-SCALAR ROW carries `at`/`over` because this task freezes its ceiling too; the
# collection rows leave them `n/a`, since the count corpus already owns their ceilings.
#
# site                      kind         zero    one     at    over  go_removal  ex_removal  owner
plan_pages_decoded          collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   retags      retags      -
plan_pages_raw              collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   silent      combined    -
plan_ranges                 collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   admits      admits      -
recovery_pages_decoded      collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   crashes     crashes     -
recovery_pages_raw          collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   silent      silent      -
recovery_spans_chain        collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   retags      retags      -
recovery_spans_single       collection   refuse  accept  n/a   n/a   retags      n/a         1.6-d
tombstone_declared_count    scalar       refuse  accept  1024  1025  admits      n/a         1.6-d
